title: If we really went to the moon in 1969, why haven't we been back since 1972? Think about it.
content:
Ok so let me get this straight. In 1969 we had computers weaker than a Tamagotchi, suits held together with basically duct tape, and rockets designed by a literal former Nazi scientist (look up Operation Paperclip, it's real) — and we NAILED IT on the first try. Six successful landings. Zero problems. Then in 1972 we just... stopped. And in the 50+ years since, with technology that is literally millions of times more powerful, we just... can't go back?

NASA themselves admitted they "destroyed the technology" and "it would be painful to build it back." Their words not mine. You don't "destroy" technology that works. You iterate on it. Unless it never existed in the first place.

Let's talk about the Van Allen radiation belts. These are bands of intense radiation surrounding Earth that should have absolutely fried the astronauts. NASA's official explanation is basically "they went through it really fast." Oh ok cool, I'll just drive through a wall really fast next time.

And the footage. Oh man, the footage. The flag "waving" in a vacuum. The multiple light sources when the sun should be the only one. The identical backgrounds in photos that were supposedly taken miles apart. The fact that the original high-quality tapes were "accidentally erased" in the 1980s. Who accidentally erases the most important footage in human history?

Stanley Kubrick released 2001: A Space Odyssey in 1968 — one year before the "landing." The man literally invented front-projection technology for that film. And then NASA just happened to pull off the real thing 12 months later looking suspiciously similar? The Shining is Kubrick's confession. Room 237. The Apollo 11 sweater on Danny. Do your own research.

I'm not saying space isn't real. I'm saying we didn't go to the moon in 1969. And the fact that they won't go back tells you everything you need to know.
source_title: Space Industry Faces Questions as Moon Mission Gap Reaches 52 Years

title: MIT did a study "debunking" tin foil hats and it was FUNDED BY THE GOVERNMENT. Do I need to draw you a picture?
content:
Every time someone brings up tin foil hats, some redditor links the MIT study from 2005 like it's the final word on the matter. "AcTuAlLy TiN fOiL hAtS aMpLiFy SiGnAlS." Yeah. That's exactly what they'd want you to think.

Let's think about this for two seconds. Who funds MIT? Federal grants. Who distributes federal grants? The government. So the government funded a study at one of their top research universities that concluded the ONE low-cost method of blocking electromagnetic signals actually makes things worse. How convenient.

And notice what they did — they didn't say "foil hats do nothing." They said foil hats AMPLIFY certain government frequencies. Translation: "Please stop wearing them, they're making our signals stronger, we definitely aren't worried about you blocking anything." That's not debunking. That's reverse psychology. That's a psy-op.

Why does every movie, every TV show, every piece of media portray tin foil hat wearers as crazy? Because it's the most effective form of discrediting in human history. You don't have to disprove the method — you just have to make anyone who uses it look insane. It costs them nothing and it works on 99% of people.

Here are things we KNOW are real: the government has technology that can beam sounds directly into your skull (look up the microwave auditory effect — it's declassified). Cell towers broadcast in the exact frequency ranges that aluminum attenuates. And the first person to write about foil hats — Julian Huxley — was the brother of Aldous Huxley, who wrote BRAVE NEW WORLD, a book about a government that controls its population's thoughts. Coincidence? COINCIDENCE?

I'm not telling you to wear a tin foil hat. I'm telling you to ask yourself why they spent so much money and cultural capital convincing you not to. That's all. Think about it.
source_title: Federal Funding of MIT Electromagnetic Study Raises Questions Among Researchers

title: I tried to drive to Bielefeld, Germany last summer. What happened next changed everything I thought I knew.
content:
So last July I was doing a road trip through Germany. Munich, Hamburg, Berlin, the usual. My buddy dared me to stop in Bielefeld because of the whole conspiracy thing. I thought it would be funny. Put it in Google Maps, got directions, started driving.

Here's where it gets weird. I was driving on the A2 autobahn, which supposedly goes right through Bielefeld. I set the GPS for the city center. About 30 km out, my GPS 'recalculated' and routed me around the city. I manually set it again. Recalculated AGAIN. I said screw it and just followed highway signs.

I saw a sign that said 'Bielefeld 15 km.' Then nothing. The next sign was for Herford. Bielefeld just... wasn't there anymore. I pulled over at a gas station and asked the attendant how to get to Bielefeld. He looked at me like I asked him where Narnia was and said 'just keep driving, you'll find it.' Helpful.

Now before you say 'you just missed the exit' -- I drove that stretch THREE TIMES. I have a master's degree. I can read highway signs. Something is not right.

And don't even get me started on the fact that the German government has NEVER officially denied the conspiracy. They joke about it. They laugh. You know what people do when they're hiding something? They make the truth sound like a joke so nobody takes it seriously.

330,000 people supposedly live there but have you EVER met someone from Bielefeld? Have you? Because I haven't. And I've been to Germany four times.

THEY don't want you asking questions. But I'm asking them anyway.
source_title: The Bielefeld Anomaly: When Satire Meets Something Stranger on Germany's Roads

title: The government has changed the Roswell story FOUR TIMES since 1947. Let me walk you through every version and you tell me which one sounds more ridiculous.
content:
Let's play a game. I'll list every official explanation the U.S. government has given for what crashed at Roswell, and you tell me if this sounds like an organization that's telling the truth.

Version 1 (July 8, 1947): The Army issues a press release saying they recovered a 'flying disc.' Their words. Not mine. Not some conspiracy website. The ACTUAL UNITED STATES MILITARY said they found a flying disc.

Version 2 (July 9, 1947): ONE DAY LATER, they change the story. Now it's a weather balloon. They hold a press conference with balloon debris that looks nothing like what the witnesses described. General Ramey literally posed for photos with substitute materials.

Version 3 (1994): After 47 years of 'weather balloon,' the Air Force suddenly says actually it was a Project Mogul balloon. A classified nuclear detection balloon. Oh so it WASN'T a weather balloon? So you lied for 47 years? Cool cool cool.

Version 4 (1997): The Air Force publishes ANOTHER report to explain the 'alien bodies' witnesses reported. Their explanation? Crash test dummies dropped from high altitude in the 1950s. Except the Roswell crash was in 1947. The dummy drops started in 1953. SIX YEARS LATER. The Air Force's official explanation is that witnesses confused events from different DECADES. That's their story.

Now let's look at what the witnesses actually said. Jesse Marcel, the intelligence officer who first examined the debris, went to his grave saying it was not from any balloon. Multiple witnesses described metallic material that couldn't be bent, cut, or burned. Brazel's son said the debris had properties unlike anything he'd ever seen.

Four stories in 50 years. Each one contradicting the last. And somehow I'M the crazy one for asking questions. They don't want you thinking about this. They want you to accept Version 4 and move on. But if they've lied three times already, why would the fourth time be the truth?

Connect the dots. Or don't. They're counting on you not to.
source_title: Defense Contractors Rally as Roswell Disclosure Debate Resurfaces in Washington

title: I don't care about politics left or right but can someone explain why they needed THREE YEARS to produce a birth certificate? Something doesn't sit right.
content:
Look I need to preface this by saying I'm not political. I don't care about Democrat vs Republican. This isn't about that. This is about asking a simple question and watching the most powerful government on earth take THREE YEARS to answer it.

2008: People ask to see the birth certificate. Simple request. Every president could do this in about five minutes. Instead we get a 'Certificate of Live Birth' which is NOT the same thing as a birth certificate. It's a short-form digital printout. Any Hawaiian could get one. It proves nothing about WHERE you were born.

2009: Still no long-form certificate. 2010: Still nothing. Media calls anyone who asks a 'conspiracy theorist.' Classic. Shut down the question instead of answering it.

April 2011: FINALLY releases the long-form birth certificate. Three years later. And it just happens to be right before the 2012 campaign season. Convenient timing.

Now here's what nobody talks about. His grandmother — his OWN grandmother in Kenya — said in a recorded interview that she was present at his birth IN KENYA. The media immediately 'debunked' this by saying it was a translation error. She spoke in Swahili and supposedly meant something different. Right. A grandmother says she saw her grandson born and we're blaming Google Translate.

And the newspaper announcements from 1961? Anyone can submit a birth announcement. His grandparents lived in Hawaii. They could have called it in from anywhere. That's not proof, that's a phone call.

I'm not saying anything definitive. I'm just saying when someone takes three years to show you an ID, maybe it's because they were working on it. Do your own research. Look at the documents yourself. Don't let the media tell you what to think.

And before you call me a conspiracy theorist — I literally just asked a question.
source_title: Questions Persist Over Three-Year Delay in Birth Certificate Release
